entities.summary: Ingeborg Magnusdotter of Sweden (c. 1290–1319) was Queen of Denmark by marriage to King Eric VI, thereby linking the Swedish and Danish crowns in a union that would last for over a century. Born in Sweden to King Magnus Ladulås and Helvig of Holstein, she was the younger sister of Magnus II of Sweden and a cousin of King Haakon V of Norway. Her marriage to Eric VI strengthened the ties between the Scandinavian kingdoms and paved the way for increased cooperation on matters of trade, security, and culture. Ingeborg's influence on her husband's policies, particularly in regards to the role of women in government and the administration of justice, would shape the course of Danish history. This legacy extends beyond the medieval period, as the institution of queenship in Denmark would continue to evolve in response to the changing needs and values of the society. Ingeborg's story is a testament to the enduring power of women in shaping the course of history, even in the face of patriarchal norms and societal expectations.
